Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 09:33:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Production: sudden throughput drop + elevated 5xx (region us-west)

Status update (initial triage):
- Scope: regression appears confined to the streaming worker pool serving long-context chat and streaming responses for model keystone-v2-large in us-west region. Non-streaming inference paths (batch/embeddings) look healthy.
- Signal: KV cache eviction increased over last hour; we see repeated cache misses resulting in backend fanout and increased kernel launches leading to tail latency.
- Hypothesis: a config change in the cache TTL that was rolled out in autoscale agent at 08:15 PT triggered higher cache churn under OrbitPay traffic patterns.

Immediate mitigations in-flight:
1) Rolling rollback of autoscale agent config to prior TTL (launched at 09:40 PT, in progress).
2) Temporarily increase worker pool capacity for keystone-v2-large by 30% (expected to reduce tail by ~50%).
3) Enable KV-prefetch flag to reduce cold misses for hotspot keys (will be enabled as a canary on two nodes at 09:55 PT).

Attaching the Keystones scaling runbook as requested. Will post more telemetry once rollback completes.

— Laura
VP Engineering, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Production: sudden throughput drop + elevated 5xx (region us-west)

Quick SRE play-by-play:
- 09:40 PT: rolled back autoscale agent TTL change across us-west (rollback complete at 09:47 PT).
- 09:50 PT: provisioned +30% worker capacity for keystone-v2-large in us-west (nodes spun up by 10:04 PT).
- 10:05 PT: enabled KV-prefetch on the two canary nodes — prefetch hit-rate improved from 18% -> 72% on canary.

Observed impact: 75th p99 latency dropped from 2.2s -> 1.1s on canaries, 5xx rate on canary traffic dropped to 0.08%. Rolling rollout to remaining nodes at 10:30 PT.

Next steps: monitor this for 2 hours; if stable we keep new capacity and mark incident as mitigated; otherwise we'll open a kernel-level investigation.

Attached: keystone-scaling-runbook.pdf (runbook excerpt).

— Hannah
Sr. SRE Manager
Redwood Inference

Date: Sat, 7 Nov 2026 11:10:00 -08:00
Subject: OrbitPay update: mitigation actions & expected timeline (for execs)

Hi Michael / Sara — quick update from Redwood: we identified a config rollout to the autoscale agent that increased KV cache churn for keystone-v2-large in us-west. Engineering rolled back the change and provisioned temporary capacity; SRE reports early signal improvement on canaries.

Current status (11:10 PT):
- Partial mitigation observed on canaries: 5xx reduced to 0.08% on canary traffic, p99 latency improved.
- Rollout to remaining nodes started at 10:30 PT.
- Expected customer-visible stabilization window: 60–90 minutes if rollouts continue without regressions.

Ask: can you confirm whether OrbitPay will pause non-essential heavy jobs (mass reconciliation) for the next 2 hours? That will make stabilization quicker.

We will send a short executive-facing update at 12:00 PT summarizing impact and ETA. Please let me know if you want additional language (credit offer / SLA note).

— Marcus Lin
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
